question_en: A 5-year-old Syrian immigrant and her family present for an immigration physical. She has no past medical history but her grandmother, age 72, was just diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast. The patient is an avid softball player at her high school and denies alcohol, smoking, or illicit drug use. On exam, the breasts appear symmetric and normal. A 3-cm round, mobile mass is palpated in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast. There is slight tenderness to deep palpation of the mass. There is no axillary lymphadenopathy on either side. Which of the following is the most likely outcome of this patient’s condition?

options_en.A: This mass will decrease in size if the patient starts oral contraceptives
options_en.B: This mass slightly increases this patient’s risk of breast cancer in the future
options_en.C: This mass will most likely decrease in size or disappear over time
options_en.D: If this mass grows rapidly to greater than 5 cm, radiation and chemotherapy are indicated

question_ru: Ek 16 saal ki khatoon apne doctor ke daftar mein aayi hai jab usne apne baen sine mein 2 mahine pehle ek gol gath mehsoos ki. Wo batati hai ke gath aakhri 2 mahawariyon se pehle barh gayi thi aur dard karne lagi thi. Warna yeh dardnahin hai, aur mareez kisi bhi discharge ya skin tabdeeli se inkaar karti hai. Uska koi pehla medical tareekh nahi hai lekin uski dadi, jo 72 saal ki hain, abhi abhi invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast ke saath tashkhis hui hai. Mareez apne high school ki ek shaukeen softball khiladi hai aur sharab, smoking, ya najaiz drugs ke istemal se inkaar karti hai. Jaanch par, sine simetrik aur normal nazar aate hain. Baen sine ke upper outer quadrant mein 3 cm ka gol, chalne wala gath mehsoos hota hai. Gath ko gehri janch par halka dard hota hai. Dono taraf axillary lymphadenopathy nahi hai. Is mareez ke halat ka sab se mumkin nataija kya ho sakta hai?

options_ru.A: Yeh massa chhota ho jayega agar mareez oral contraceptives lena shuru kar de.
options_ru.B: Yeh mass is mareez ke mustaqbil mein breast cancer ke khatrey ko thoda barha deta hai.
options_ru.C: Yeh mass aksar waqt ke sath size mein kam ya gayab ho jata hai.
options_ru.D: Agar yeh mass tezi se barh kar 5 cm se zyada ho jaye, to radiation aur chemotherapy zaroori hoti hai.

A 57-year-old homeless man is brought to the emergency department because of several episodes of hematemesis in the past 24 hours. His vital signs include a temperature of 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse of 95/min, and blood pressure of 85/60 mm Hg. On physical examination, he appears confused and unable to give a complete history. He is noted to have jaundice, palpable firm liver, mild splenomegaly, and shifting dullness consistent with the presence of ascites. Liver function tests are as follows:
Serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST)  97 U/L
Serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 40 U/L
Serum albumin 2.5 g/dL
Total bilirubin 3 mg/dL
Prothrombin time 20 seconds
Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's illness?
question_ru:
Ek 57 saal ka beghar mard emergency department mein laya gaya hai kyun ke usne pichlay 24 ghanton mein kai martaba hematemesis ki hai. Uske vital signs mein temperature 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse 95/min, aur blood pressure 85/60 mm Hg hai. Jismani jaayza mein, woh mutasir nazar aata hai aur mukammal tareekh dene se qasir hai. Us mein peela pan (jaundice), mehsoos hone wala sakht jigar, halka sa spleen ka phailna (mild splenomegaly), aur shifting dullness jo ascites ke mojoodgi se mutabiq hai, dekha gaya hai. Liver function tests kuch yun hain:
Serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST)  97 U/L

Serum albumin 2.5 g/dL

question_en:
A 54-year-old male presents to his primary care physician complaining of fatigue. He reports that he recently went on a vacation to South America with his family but just wanted to stay in his hotel all day due to fatigue. His past medical history is notable for hyperlipidemia and hypertension. He takes lovastatin and lisinopril. He drinks socially and has a 20 pack-year smoking history. His temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 130/75 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, and respirations are 16/min. On exam, the patient is appropriately interactive and in no acute distress. Mild splenomegaly is noted. Laboratory analysis reveals the following:

Hemoglobin: 11.0 g/dL
Hematocrit: 36%
Leukocyte count: 3,800/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 140,000/mm^3

A bone marrow aspiration is ordered but after multiple attempts, they are unable to obtain an adequate bone marrow sample. A peripheral blood smear would likely reveal cells that stain with which of the following stains?
question_ru:
Ek 54 saal ka mard apne primary care physician ke paas thakan ki shikayat ke sath aata hai. Wo batata hai ke wo haal hi mein apne khandan ke sath South America chhutti par gaya tha lekin thakan ki wajah se poora din apne hotel mein rehna chahta tha. Uski medical history mein hyperlipidemia aur hypertension shamil hain. Wo lovastatin aur lisinopril leta hai. Wo samaji taur par sharab peeta hai aur uska 20 pack-saal smoking ka record hai. Uska temperature 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure 130/75 mmHg, pulse 80/min, aur saanson ki tadaad 16/min hai. Jaanch mein, mareez munasib taur par interactive hai aur kisi shiddat wali takleef mein nahi hai. Halka sa spleen bara hona note kiya gaya hai. Laboratory analysis mein ye natije mile hain:

Hemoglobin: 11.0 g/dL
Hematocrit: 36%
Leukocyte count: 3,800/mm^3 normal differential ke sath
Platelet count: 140,000/mm^3

Bone marrow aspiration ka order diya gaya lekin kai koshishon ke bawajood wo kafi bone marrow sample hasil nahi kar sake. Peripheral blood smear mein aise cells nazar aayenge jo kin stains ke sath stain hote hain?

question_en: While on a teaching sabbatical in Uruguay, a pathologist examined the excised liver of an 18-year-old otherwise healthy female who passed away due to massive hepatic necrosis 5 days after she underwent general anesthesia to repair a fractured femur. Which of the following is a general anesthetic most likely responsible for her death?

question_en: A 45-year-old woman with hypothyroidism comes to the physician because of progressive fatigue, lethargy, and epigastric pain after eating. Physical examination shows pale conjunctivae. Laboratory studies show decreased serum hemoglobin levels and increased serum gastrin levels. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy shows inflammation of the gastric body and fundus. A photomicrograph of a biopsy specimen taken from the gastric antrum is shown. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?
question_ru: Ek 45 saal ki aurat jo hypothyroidism ki mareez hai, doctor ke paas aati hai barhti hui thakan, susti, aur khanay ke baad epigastric dard ki shikayat ke sath. Jismani imtehan mein pale conjunctivae nazar aate hain. Laboratory tests mein serum hemoglobin ki satah kam aur serum gastrin ki satah zyada paayi gayi hai. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy mein gastric body aur fundus mein soozish dekhi gayi hai. Gastric antrum se li gayi biopsy specimen ki photomicrograph dikhayi gayi hai. In mein se kaun si wajah is mareez ke alamat ki sab se mumkin wajah hai?

question_en: An investigator is studying traumatic knee joint injuries in college athletes. Images and tissue samples are collected from 4 athletes with cartilaginous injury and 4 athletes with bone fractures. After 8 weeks, the athletes with bone fractures show almost complete resolution, while the athletes with cartilaginous injuries show only minimal signs of healing. The investigator hypothesizes that this is due to the absence of progenitor cells for matrix regeneration. Transplant of which of the following tissues would most likely promote healing in the group with cartilaginous injury?
question_ru: Ek tahqiqi karne wala college ke khilariyon mein traumatic ghutne ke joint ke zakhamat ka mutala kar raha hai. Tasaveer aur tissue ke samples 4 khilariyon se liye gaye jin mein cartilage ka zakham tha aur 4 khilariyon se jin mein haddiyon ke fracture thay. 8 hafton ke baad, haddiyon ke fracture wale khilariyon mein taqreeban mukammal shifa nazar aayi, jabke cartilage ke zakham wale khilariyon mein sirf thodi si shifa ke nishan nazar aaye. Tahqiqi karne wale ne yeh farziya lagaya hai ke yeh matrix ki dobara tamiir ke liye progenitor cells ki adam mojoodgi ki wajah se hai. Kin tissues ka transplant sab se zyada mumkin hai ke cartilage ke zakham wale group mein shifa ko barhawa de?

question_en: A 22-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by police after he was found undressing himself outside in 110°F weather. The patient refuses to answer any questions as he suspects that his care team is spying on him. The patient recently started college and has presented to the emergency department once before for polysubstance intoxication. The patient attempts to assault a nurse, is restrained, and given diphenhydramine and haloperidol. When the patient is able to be examined, he is somnolent and non-responsive. His temperature is 104°F (40°C), blood pressure is 147/98 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. He does not comply with any commands, and it is not possible to freely manipulate his extremities due to rigidity. His mucous membranes are dry. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
question_ru: Ek 22 saal ka mard police ke zariye emergency department mein laya gaya hai jab use 110°F mausam mein bahar kapde utarte hue paya gaya. Mareez kisi bhi sawal ka jawab dene se inkaar karta hai kyun ke use shak hai ke uski care team us par jasoosi kar rahi hai. Mareez ne haal hi mein college shuru kiya hai aur pehle bhi ek dafa emergency department mein polysubstance intoxication ke liye aaya tha. Mareez ne ek nurse par hamla karne ki koshish ki, use rok diya gaya, aur diphenhydramine aur haloperidol diye gaye. Jab mareez ka imtehan kiya gaya to wo neend mein tha aur jawab nahi de raha tha. Uska temperature 104°F (40°C), blood pressure 147/98 mmHg, pulse 120/min, saanson ki raftar 17/min, aur oxygen saturation 98% room air par tha. Wo kisi bhi hukam ki pabandi nahi karta, aur uski haddiyan sakht hone ki wajah se uske haath pair ko asani se hilaya nahi ja sakta. Uske mucous membranes sookhe hue hain. In mein se sab se mumkin tashkhees kya hai?

question_en: An 18-month-old boy is brought to his pediatrician because his mother is concerned about his walking. The boy was born at 37 weeks’ gestation and spent 1 night in the neonatal intensive care unit for respiratory distress. He otherwise has been healthy and started walking independently at 12 months. However, his mother reports that he has stopped walking and appears weaker than he was a few months ago. He also has started having brief convulsive episodes over the past week. His parents are both healthy with no medical conditions. On exam, the child demonstrates muscle rigidity and diffuse muscle wasting. He is unable to stand or sit up straight. His patellar, Achilles, and brachioradialis reflexes are absent. Fundoscopic examination is unremarkable. A urine sample demonstrates metachromic granules. This patient’s condition is caused by a defect in which of the following enzymes?
question_ru: Ek 18 mahine ka larka apne pediatrician ke paas laya gaya hai kyun ke uski maa uske chalne ke bare mein fikrmand hai. Larka 37 hafton ki gestation par paida hua tha aur respiratory distress ki wajah se neonatal intensive care unit mein 1 raat guzarai. Warna woh sehatmand raha hai aur 12 mahine ki umar mein khud se chalna shuru kiya tha. Lekin uski maa ne bataya ke usne chalna band kar diya hai aur woh chand mahine pehle se kamzor lagta hai. Usne pichle haftay se mukhtasir jhatkon ke episodes bhi shuru kar diye hain. Uske walidain dono sehatmand hain aur unhein koi medical masail nahi hain. Jaanch mein, bacha muscle rigidity aur puray jism mein muscle wasting dikhata hai. Woh khara nahi ho sakta aur seedha baith nahi sakta. Uske patellar, Achilles, aur brachioradialis reflexes maujood nahi hain. Fundoscopic imtehan normal hai. Peshab ke sample mein metachromic granules paye gaye hain. Is mareez ki halat kis enzyme ke defect ki wajah se hoti hai?

question_en: A 24-year-old woman delivers a baby at term. The Apgar counts are 9 and 10 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. Thirty minutes after delivery, the mother’s blood pressure drops to 80/60 mm Hg and her pulse is 124/min. On physical examination, her distal extremities are clammy and cold, and the uterus is boggy. Aggressive fluid resuscitation is initiated. After administering 4 units of IV fluids and 4 units of whole blood, her vitals stabilize. The next morning, she says she is unable to lactate when she tries to breastfeed her child. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the failure of lactation in this patient?
question_ru: Ek 24 saal ki aurat ne term par bacha paida kiya. Apgar scores 1 aur 5 minute par mutadid tor par 9 aur 10 hain. Paidaish ke 30 minute baad, maa ka blood pressure 80/60 mm Hg tak gir jata hai aur uski pulse 124/min hai. Jismani jaiza lene par, uske haathon aur paon thanday aur pasine se bheegay huay hain, aur uterus narm aur phoola hua hai. Shadeed fluid resuscitation shuru ki jati hai. 4 units IV fluids aur 4 units whole blood dene ke baad, uske vitals mustahkam ho jate hain. Agle din subah, woh kehti hai ke jab woh apne bache ko doodh pilane ki koshish karti hai to doodh nahi nikalta. Is mareez mein doodh na nikalne ki sab se mumkin wajah kya hai?

options_ru.B: bachadani mein placenta ke baaqi hisson

question_en: A 27-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for a general checkup. She has been doing well in school and has no complaints. The patient has a past medical history of asthma which is controlled with albuterol. She is currently sexually active but states that she uses birth control. She has many friends and states that her mood is typically positive. The patient's last pap smear was 1 year ago. Her father died of colon cancer at the age of 68, and her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer at the age of 65. Her temperature is 98.7°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 147/108 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. The patient's BMI is 19 kg/m^2. Physical exam demonstrates a normal S1 and S2, normal breath sounds, and an abdominal exam that is within normal limits. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

options_en.B: Discontinue birth control and place an intrauterine device

question_ru: Ek 27 saal ki aurat apne primary care physician ke paas general checkup ke liye aayi hai. Wo school mein achi kar rahi hai aur koi shikayat nahi hai. Mareez ki medical history mein asthma hai jo albuterol se control mein hai. Wo filhaal sexually active hai lekin kehti hai ke wo birth control istemal karti hai. Uske bohat se dost hain aur wo kehti hai ke uska mood aam tor par positive rehta hai. Mareez ka aakhri pap smear 1 saal pehle hua tha. Uske walid 68 saal ki umar mein colon cancer se mar chuke hain, aur uski walida ko 65 saal ki umar mein breast cancer diagnose hua tha. Uska temperature 98.7°F (37.1°C), blood pressure 147/108 mmHg, pulse 80/min, respirations 15/min, aur oxygen saturation 99% room air par hai. Mareez ka BMI 19 kg/m^2 hai. Physical exam mein normal S1 aur S2, normal breath sounds, aur abdominal exam normal limits mein hai. Management mein agla behtareen qadam kya hoga?

question_en: A 24-year-old primigravida presents to her physician at 20 weeks gestation. question_en:
A 3-day-old male is evaluated in the hospital nursery for delayed passage of meconium. His mother is breastfeeding and has started to produce milk. The patient has been feeding well every two hours and is urinating over eight times per day. The patient was born at 35 weeks gestation to a 27-year-old gravida 4. The pregnancy was uncomplicated until the patient’s mother had spontaneous rupture of membranes at 35 weeks gestation. The patient’s three older siblings are all healthy. In the hospital nursery, the patient’s temperature is 98.2°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 48/32 mmHg, pulse is 164/min, and respirations are 48/min. Hamila asan thi jab tak mareez ki maa ke membranes 35 haftay ki haibaat par khud ba khud phat nahi gaye. Mareez ke teen bade bhai behen tamam sehatmand hain. Hospital nursery mein mareez ka darja hararat 98.2°F (36.8°C), khoon ka dabao 48/32 mmHg, pulse 164/min, aur saanson ki raftaar 48/min hai. If these waste products are not cleared by the liver and kidneys, hyperammonemia can occur, leading to confusion and delirium. options_en.C: Citrulline + aspartate + ATP --> arginosuccinate + AMP + PPi

question_ru: Protein ke normal catabolism ke dauran, urea aur ammonia waste products ke tor par paida hotay hain. Khushkismati se, sehatmand jigar in waste products ko urea cycle ke zariye saaf kar sakta hai. In mein se kaun sa reaction is cycle ka rate limiting step hai?

question_en: An 18-year-old male is brought in by fire rescue. The patient was an unrestrained passenger in a motor vehicle crash and was ejected from the vehicle after collision. Radiographs of his lower extremity show multiple long bone fractures. Two large bore IV lines are placed, and the patient oozes from around the sites of venepuncture. Labs are notable for a WBC of 20,000/mm^3, Hb of 10.1g/dL, platelets of 48,000/mm^3, and prolongation of the PT and aPTT. question_en: Two hours following an elective cholecystectomy, a 43-year-old woman has fever and chills. question_en: A 33-year-old man presents to the emergency department with altered mental status. He was at work as a construction worker when his coworkers found him down at the work site. He also has a past medical history of schizophrenia well controlled with haloperidol and is currently taking phenytoin for epilepsy. He is also currently taking propranolol for anxiety and hyperthyroidism. His temperature is 106°F (41.1°C), blood pressure is 109/62 mmHg, pulse is 170/min, respirations are 23/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical exam is notable for an altered man with a Glasgow Coma Scale of 10. He has minimal muscle tone and is incoherent when answering questions. The patient is covered in sweat and dirt. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

question_en:
Sauna use, sometimes referred to as "sauna bathing," is characterized by short-term passive exposure to extreme heat. This exposure elicits mild hyperthermia – an increase in the body's core temperature – that induces a thermoregulatory response involving neuroendocrine, cardiovascular, and cytoprotective mechanisms that work together to restore homeostasis and condition the body for future heat stressors… In recent decades, sauna bathing has emerged as a means to increase lifespan and improve overall health, based on compelling data from observational, interventional, and mechanistic studies. Of particular interest are the findings from studies of participants in the Kuopio Ischemic Heart Disease Risk Factor (KIHD) Study, an ongoing prospective population-based cohort study of health outcomes in more than 2,300 middle-aged men from eastern Finland, which identified strong links between sauna use and reduced death and disease… The KIHD findings showed that men who used the sauna two to three times per week were 27 percent less likely to die from cardiovascular-related causes than men who didn't use the sauna.[2] Furthermore, the benefits they experienced were found to be dose-dependent: Men who used the sauna roughly twice as often, about four to seven times per week, experienced roughly twice the benefits – and were 50 percent less likely to die from cardiovascular-related causes.[2] In addition, frequent sauna users were found to be 40 percent less likely to die from all causes of premature death. These findings held true even when considering age, activity levels, and lifestyle factors that might have influenced the men's health.[2]... The KIHD also revealed that frequent sauna use reduced the risk of developing dementia and Alzheimer's disease in a dose-dependent manner. Men who used the sauna two to three times per week had a 66 percent lower risk of developing dementia and a 65 percent lower risk of developing Alzheimer's disease, compared to men who used the sauna only one time per week… The health benefits associated with sauna use extended to other aspects of mental health, as well. Men participating in the KIHD study who used the sauna four to seven times per week were 77 percent less likely to develop psychotic disorders, regardless of the men's dietary habits, socioeconomic status, physical activity, and inflammatory status (as measured by C-reactive protein)…Exposure to high temperature stresses the body, eliciting a rapid, robust response. The skin and core body temperatures increase markedly, and sweating ensues. The skin heats first, rising to 40°C (104°F), and then changes in core body temperature occur, rising slowly from 37°C (98.6°F, or normal) to 38°C (100.4°F) and then rapidly increasing to 39°C (102.2°F)…  Cardiac output, a measure of the amount of work the heart performs in response to the body's need for oxygen, increases by 60 to 70 percent, while the heart rate (the number of beats per minute) increases and the stroke volume (the amount of blood pumped) remains unchanged.[5] During this time, approximately 50 to 70 percent of the body's blood flow is redistributed from the core to the skin to facilitate sweating. The average person loses approximately 0.5 kg of sweat while sauna bathing.[11] Acute heat exposure also induces a transient increase in overall plasma volume to mitigate the decrease in core blood volume. This increase in plasma volume not only provides a reserve source of fluid for sweating, but it also acts like the water in a car's radiator, cooling the body to prevent rapid increases in core body temperature and promoting heat tolerance… Repeated sauna use acclimates the body to heat and optimizes the body's response to future exposures, likely due to a biological phenomenon known as hormesis, a compensatory defense response following exposure to a mild stressor that is disproportionate to the magnitude of the stressor. Hormesis triggers a vast array of protective mechanisms that not only repair cell damage but also provide protection from subsequent exposures to more devastating stressors… The physiological responses to sauna use are remarkably similar to those experienced during moderate- to vigorous-intensity exercise. In fact, sauna use has been proposed as an alternative to exercise for people who are unable to engage in physical activity due to chronic disease or physical limitations.[13]

Based on the article, what would be an important thing for a person to do after sauna use?

question_en: A 78-year-old male presents to the office with the complaint of severe neck pain. He rates the pain as a 7 on a scale of 0 to 10 scale. He denies any trauma but reports that he had been doing a lot of painting over the past week. He denies any radicular pain or numbness. Cervical range of motion is moderately limited in all fields. He is treated with articulatory springing technique. Four hours later the physician receives a call from the local emergency department, where the patient presented confused, nauseated, and vertiginous. The physician may be found liable if

options_en.A: the motion barrier was articulated more than 3 times
options_en.B: the motion barrier was met with a vectored force from the direction of ease
options_en.C: the neck was treated in simultaneous hyperrotation and extension
options_en.D: the patient was previously treated for osteoarthritis of the cervical spine

question_ru: Ek 78 saal ka mard daftar mein shikayat ke sath aata hai ke uske gardan mein shadid dard hai. Woh dard ko 0 se 10 ke scale par 7 batata hai. Woh kisi chot se inkaar karta hai magar batata hai ke pichle hafte mein usne bohat painting ki hai. Woh kisi radicular dard ya sunpan se inkaar karta hai. Gardan ki harkat har simt mein darmiyani had tak mehdood hai. Uska ilaaj articulatory springing technique se kiya jata hai. Char ghante baad doctor ko local emergency department se call aata hai jahan mareez uljhan, matli aur chakkar ki shikayat ke sath pesh hua. Doctor zimmedar thaharaaya ja sakta hai agar

options_ru.A: motion barrier ko 3 se zyada dafa wazeh kiya gaya tha
options_ru.B: motion barrier ko asani ki simt se ek vectored force ka samna hua
options_ru.C: gardan ko ek saath hyperrotation aur extension mein treat kiya gaya tha
options_ru.D: mareez ko pehle gardan ki haddi ke osteoarthritis ka ilaaj kiya gaya tha

question_en: A 71-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her daughter for evaluation of her mental status. The daughter says, "I visited Mom today for the first time in 6 months; her memory has worsened, her bills are unpaid, and her house is unusually messy." The patient says, "I'm perfectly healthy." Medical history is significant for hypertension diagnosed more than 25 years ago, and two small strokes occurring 3 years and 7 months ago. The daughter gives you three empty medicine bottles from her mother's home: metoprolol, hydrochlorothiazide, and aspirin. The patient is 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weighs 59 kg (130 lb); BMI is 22 kg/m2 . Vital signs are temperature 36.4°C (97.6°F), pulse 76/min, respirations 16/min, and blood pressure 196/112 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 93%. Muscle strength in her left hand is 1/5. Strength in the right extremities is 4/5. The patient is oriented only to self; she does not know the day of the week or today's date. She recalls 0 of 3 words at 5 minutes, and she is unable to name 2 objects, correctly draw interlocking pentagons, or count backwards by serial sevens. Complete blood count, renal function studies, liver function studies, and urinalysis are all within the reference ranges. ECG shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of the patient's symptoms?
question_ru: Ek 71 saal ki aurat ko uski beti emergency department mein uske zehni haal ke jaayze ke liye laya gaya hai. Beti kehti hai, "Main aaj pehli dafa 6 mahine baad Ammi se mili; unki yaadash kamzor ho gayi hai, unke bill ada nahi hue hain, aur unka ghar ajeeb tareeke se ganda hai." Mareez kehti hai, "Main bilkul sehatmand hoon." Tibbi tareekh mein 25 saal se zyada pehle tashkhis shuda hypertension aur 3 saal aur 7 mahine pehle do chhoti strokes shamil hain. Beti aapko apni maa ke ghar se teen khaali dawa ke bottle deti hai: metoprolol, hydrochlorothiazide, aur aspirin. Mareez ki lambai 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) hai aur wazan 59 kg (130 lb); BMI 22 kg/m2 hai. Vital signs hain temperature 36.4°C (97.6°F), pulse 76/min, saanson ki raftaar 16/min, aur blood pressure 196/112 mm Hg. Room air par pulse oximetry oxygen saturation 93% dikhata hai. Uske baen haath ki muscle taqat 1/5 hai. Daen haath aur paon ki taqat 4/5 hai. Mareez sirf apne aap ko samajhti hai; use hafta ka din ya aaj ki tareekh pata nahi. Woh 5 minute baad 3 alfaaz mein se koi bhi yaad nahi kar pati, aur woh 2 ashya ke naam nahi le sakti, sahi tareeke se interlocking pentagons nahi bana pati, aur serial sevens mein peeche nahi gin sakti. Mukammal khoon ki jaanch, gurday ki function ki jaanch, jigar ki function ki jaanch, aur urine ki jaanch sab normal hain. ECG mein koi kharabi nahi hai. Mareez ke symptoms ki sab se mumkina bunyadi wajah kya hai?

question_en: A previously healthy 15-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department in August 1 hour after the onset of headache, dizziness, nausea, and one episode of vomiting. question_en: A 2-year-old boy is brought to the office by his mother for follow-up of a chromosome analysis done 1 month ago. The child has minor dysmorphic features, and growth and developmental delay. Chromosome analysis showed a small unbalanced chromosome translocation, with extra chromosomal material at the tip of chromosome 3. The cytogenetics laboratory requested blood samples from both parents for follow-up studies. The parents are divorced, and the mother has custody of the child. The relationship between the parents is hostile. The mother has been tested and has normal chromosomes without evidence of translocation. At today's visit, she reacts angrily when the issue of contacting the child's father for testing is raised. She states that he abandoned them and that he has no interest in his child. She refuses to cooperate in contacting the father, who could be a translocation carrier. You do not know the father, but an office worker told you that he lives in a nearby town. The mother says that he is living with a new girlfriend. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options_en.A: Attempt to identify the father's physician and work with that physician to obtain chromosome studies on the father
options_en.B: Contact the father by telephone and arrange for him to give a blood sample at a local hospital
options_en.C: Document your attempts to work with the mother but proceed no further, since you have no physician-patient relationship with the father
options_en.D: Help the mother deal with her anger and educate her regarding the potential benefit to her son and others if the father's chromosome studies are done

question_ru: Ek 2 saal ka larka apni maa ke saath office laya gaya hai chromosome analysis ke follow-up ke liye jo 1 mahina pehle hua tha. Bachay mein halka sa dysmorphic features hain, aur growth aur developmental delay hai. Chromosome analysis ne ek chhoti unbalanced chromosome translocation dikhayi, jisme chromosome 3 ke tip par extra chromosomal material hai. Cytogenetics laboratory ne dono walidain se khoon ke samples maange hain follow-up studies ke liye. Walidain talaaq shuda hain, aur maa ke paas bache ki custody hai. Walidain ke darmiyan rishta dushmanana hai. Maa ka test hua hai aur uske chromosomes normal hain bina kisi translocation ke saboot ke. Aaj ki visit par, jab bache ke walid se testing ke liye raabta karne ki baat ki gayi to woh gusse mein aayi. Usne kaha ke usne unhein chhor diya hai aur uska apne bache mein koi dilchaspi nahi hai. Woh walid se raabta karne mein taawun karne se inkaar karti hai, jo ke translocation carrier ho sakta hai. Aap walid ko nahi jaante, magar ek office worker ne bataya ke woh qareebi shehar mein rehta hai. Maa kehti hai ke woh apni nayi girlfriend ke saath rehta hai. In mein se sab se munasib agla qadam kya hoga?

options_ru.A: Koshish karein ke walid ke doctor ka pata lagaya jaye aur us doctor ke saath mil kar walid ke chromosome ke mutaliq studies hasil ki jayein.
options_ru.B: Waldain se telephone par raabta karein aur un se kaha jaye ke wo ek maqami hospital mein khoon ka sample dein.
options_ru.C: Apni koshishon ko document karein ke aap ne maa ke saath kaam kiya, magar aage na badhein, kyun ke aap ka baap ke saath physician-patient rishta nahi hai.
options_ru.D: Ammi ki gussa samajhne mein madad karein aur unhein taleem dein ke agar walid ke chromosome ke mutaliq mutalaat kiye jayein to unke bete aur doosron ke liye kya faida ho sakta hai.

question_en: A 38-year-old man with Down syndrome and severe mental retardation is brought to the emergency department by ambulance because of increasing lethargy for the past several hours. The patient is noncommunicative and you are unable to obtain an initial history of his present illness or a past medical history. You do not know if he takes any medications. Vital signs are temperature 38.3°C (100.9°F), pulse 90/min, respirations 19/min, and blood pressure 120/60 mm Hg. On physical examination the patient is awake but lethargic. Auscultation of the chest discloses clear lungs; cardiac examination discloses a systolic click. Neurologic examination shows decreased muscle tone. Serum electrolyte concentrations are normal. Complete blood count shows a leukocyte count of 18,000/mm3 with 23% band neutrophils. The patient's caregiver, who is also the patient's guardian, cannot be located and staff at the group home where the patient resides cannot be reached by telephone. The patient refuses lumbar puncture for examination of cerebrospinal fluid. Toxicologic screening of the urine is negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options_en.B: Await contact with the caregiver before proceeding with management
options_en.C: Obtain CT scan of the head

question_ru: Ek 38 saal ka mard jise Down syndrome aur shadeed zehni kamzoori hai, ambulance ke zariye emergency department mein laya gaya hai kyun ke pichle chand ghanton se uski susti barh rahi hai. Mareez baat nahi kar sakta aur aap uski maujooda bemari ya guzri hui tibbi tareekh hasil nahi kar pa rahe. Aapko maloom nahi ke wo koi dawa le raha hai ya nahi.
